title: Virome DNA Extraction with Phenol-Chloroform
author: Adair Borges
materials: To degrade any non-encapsulated nucleic acids, treat the concentrated phage lysate with 10 µg/mL RNase A (NEB T3018) and 10 µg/mL DNase I (NEB M0303). Digest for 1 h at room temperature or 4 °C overnight. Store phage at 4 °C.
Strip away phage capsids with 1 µl of Proteinase K (NEB P8107S) + 0.05% SDS. Incubate at 55 °C for 60 min on a Thermomixer at 250 rpm. If you only have a static heat block, vortex every 10 min.

In fume hood, add an equal volume of phenol – chloroform – isoamyl alcohol mixture, pH 8 (Sigma Aldrich 77618) to the digested phage. If the volume of phage is low, consider bringing up the volume to 500 µl with 1× TE buffer. Incubate at room temperature for 10 min, vortexing regularly to keep phenol mixed in.

steps.title: Initial Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform chloroform extraction in a fume hood to isolate the aqueous layer.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous layer (top layer) to a new tube, avoiding the interface and any debris or organics.
Add an equal volume of chloroform to the sample and invert to mix.
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 5 min.
Repeat the transfer and chloroform extraction process to further purify the aqueous layer.

steps.title: DNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA using sodium acetate and isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous layer to a new tube (subsequent steps can be performed on the benchtop).
Add a 10% volume of 3 M sodium acetate and an equal volume of isopropanol to the sample.
If low DNA yield is anticipated, add glycogen (e.g., GlycoBlue, ThermoFischer AM9515) as a coprecipitant at 50–150 µg/mL.
Invert to mix and incubate at 4 °C for 2 h (or overnight).
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 30 minutes.

steps.title: DNA Pellet Recovery
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant to isolate the DNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette off and discard the liquid, leaving the DNA (which appears as a glassy smear or pellet on the side of the tube).

steps.title: Ethanol Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet with 70% ethanol to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 1 mL freshly made 70% ethanol (room temperature).
Ensure DNA is not stuck to the tube sides; if so, wash it down with the 70% EtOH.
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 5 min.
Carefully pipette off and discard the liquid.
Wash again with 500 µl of 70% ethanol.
Spin the sample at maximum speed at 4 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Ethanol Removal and Drying
steps.instruction: Completely remove residual ethanol and dry the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette off and discard the liquid.
Perform short spins and use progressively smaller pipette volumes until all ethanol is removed.
Let the pellet dry for 5 min or less.

steps.title: DNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in nuclease-free water.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 30 µl of nuclease-free water (adjust volume if a large DNA yield is anticipated).
Optionally warm the sample to 50 °C to aid resuspension.

steps.title: Quality Control and Quantification
steps.instruction: Assess the purity and quantity of the extracted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Use Nanodrop to assess contamination.
Use Qbit or Tapestation to quantify DNA yield.
